newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates steady but chartering thin.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates steady but chartering thin.

text.p: Crude oil tanker rates were steady on Friday for large vessels plying Mideast/Japan routes while 70,000 tonners moving from the Caribs to the U.S. Gulf were slightly firmer, shipping brokers said.
But overall chartering activity was rather lacklustre, and brokers said they thought many fixtures for the Christmas period had already been made.

Another three 250,000 tonne Very large Crude Carriers (VLCCs) were fixed from the Mideast to Japan, two at W61-W63. Hanhwa also fixed the 275,000 tonne Grand Lady from the Mideast to South Korea at W57.5.
Brokers said this rate would still be apropriate for slightly smaller VLCCs.
Continued enquiry in the Caribbean pushed rates above W150 and at least three fixtures were seen for 70,000 tonne vessels at around W152.5.
One ship, the Unisina, was fixed from the U.S. Gulf to Asia, with UK/Cont options, at $1.25 million/W85.
Rates for 80,000 tonners sailing across the Uk/Cont region were steady and enquiry for tonnage continued scant.
Rates for 80,000 tonne Aframaxes moving cross-Med were flat to up. Four December-loading cargoes were fixed at W110.
Fuel oil rates were slightly stronger for small ships moving from the Baltics to the UK/Cont region, reflecting a perception that ice may soon make Baltic routes harder to navigate.
Petroleum's fixture of the 25,000 tonne Pink Star at W205 from Klaipeda to the Uk/Cont was seen as representative of, or perhaps a couple of points above, the current market.

Shipbrokers said three 17,000 dwt ice-strengthened vessels, the Travestern, the Rheinstern and the Alsterstern, had been time-chartered over the winter period and were expected to be used to ferry Russian fuel from Talinn and St.Petersburg.
